paper_metadata.title: High-temperature age-hardening of a novel cost-effective Fe45Ni25Cr25Mo5 high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: Considering the high potential of age-hardening in metastable non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs), the high-temperature aging behaviour of a newly developed cost-effective Fe45Ni25Cr25Mo5 HEA with a face-centered cubic (FCC) matrix was investigated.

The Fe-enriched HEA was prepared in an arc-melting furnace using a water-cooled copper mould in an argon atmosphere. Commercial metal powders (Fe, Ni, Cr and Mo) with 99.9 wt% purity were mixed according to the designed compositions and mechanically agitated for half an hour to ensure homogeneity. Then the blended powders were compacted into small cylinders of 14 mm in diameter and 20 mm long. To ensure the chemical homogeneity, these cylinders was remelted four times with processing parameters of 250 A current and 28.5 V voltage.

bar ingots of the Fe-enriched HEA with a dimension of about 120 × 12 × 8 mm were cut into about 2 mm thick plates for aging treatments over a temperature range from 600 °C to 1000 °C for 4 to 96 h. All the aged samples were then water quenched.
